events.headline: G7 Foreign Ministers Warn China's Military Activity Near Taiwan Threatens Stability
events.summary: G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris issued a joint statement warning that China's increasingly assertive military activity east of Taiwan threatens regional stability and freedom of navigation. The statement, the strongest unified G7 position yet on the issue, follows large-scale Chinese naval drills on November 9-10 that Taiwan believes were a rehearsal for a maritime blockade.

events.headline: US Envoys Meet Putin in Moscow, Then Brief Zelensky in Dublin on Peace Talks
events.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Moscow on the morning of November 12, 2026, to discuss POW releases, aid and a multilateral peace format following the Abu Dhabi negotiating round. They then flew to Dublin the same day to debrief Ukrainian President Zelensky, who was attending the European Political Community summit.

events.headline: Iran Warns It Will 'Rain Down Hell' if US Resumes Strikes Amid Qeshm Island Tensions
events.summary: Iran threatened to retaliate forcefully if the US resumes military strikes, following earlier US action near Qeshm Island. The US has evacuated aircraft from a second UK base as tensions between Washington and Tehran persist.

events.headline: ADF Militants Kill 33 Civilians in DRC Raid, Scattering Ebola Patients and Risking Further Spread
events.summary: Islamist ADF militants killed at least 33 civilians in a raid in North Kivu's Cantine-Aloya area, forcing Ebola patients to flee treatment centers. Health officials fear the disruption could worsen an outbreak that has already killed over 5,000 people across the DRC, Kenya and Nigeria.
events.locationName: North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo

events.headline: Nvidia Shares Plunge Amid Reports Board Weighs CEO Jensen Huang's Future
events.summary: Nvidia shares fell roughly 8-9% after reports that the company's board is discussing CEO Jensen Huang's position amid allegations including purported ties to Chinese intelligence. The board reportedly discussed contingency plans for an interim CEO.

events.headline: COP31 World Leaders' Summit Opens in Antalya as Climate Talks Enter Key Phase
events.summary: The COP31 World Leaders' Summit opened in Antalya, Turkey, bringing heads of state into climate negotiations that are scheduled to run through November 20. The summit follows the formal opening of the broader UN climate conference earlier in the week.

events.headline: Haiti Hunger Crisis Deepens: Nearly 6 Million Face Severe Food Insecurity
events.summary: A new IPC analysis finds 5.94 million Haitians face severe food insecurity amid spreading gang violence and high food prices. The World Food Programme says it needs $78 million to sustain operations through March 2027.

events.headline: Houthis Capture Al-Majza'a in Lahej as Airstrike on Taiz Market Kills About 30
events.summary: Airstrikes hit the al-Hadara market in al-Waziyah, Taiz, killing at least 30 people; Houthi officials blamed Saudi-led coalition aircraft, while the Yemeni government blamed a Houthi ballistic missile and called it a war crime. Separately, Houthi forces captured the town of Al-Majza'a in Lahej Governorate, expanding their territorial control.

events.headline: Alaska US Senate Race: Peltola Extends Lead Over Sullivan Ahead of Ranked-Choice Tabulation
events.summary: With about 245,470 first-choice ballots counted (roughly 84% of expected total), Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan 48.8% to 47.1%, a roughly 4,250-vote margin. Since neither candidate cleared 50%, the race heads to Alaska's official ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18, a contest with national implications for Senate control.

events.headline: DR Congo Cholera Outbreak Called Worst in Decades, Spreads Toward Kinshasa
events.summary: The WHO reports more than 60,000 cholera cases and about 1,800 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo since the start of 2026, calling it the country's worst outbreak in decades. Fresh cases are now emerging near the outskirts of Kinshasa after the outbreak was earlier concentrated in South Kivu, North Kivu and Haut-Katanga provinces.

events.headline: Simultaneous El Niño and La Niña Flooding Displaces Over 158,000 Across Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia
events.summary: El Niño-driven Paraná and Uruguay River flooding has forced mass evacuations across northeastern Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, while La Niña-driven rains simultaneously flood much of Colombia. Combined, the disasters have displaced more than 158,000 people and killed at least 16; Argentina's Entre Ríos province saw the Uruguay River reach its highest level in nearly a century.

events.headline: Pope Leo XIV Draws Record 2.5 Million to Buenos Aires Mass, Urges Milei to Protect Vulnerable
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV concluded his Argentina visit with a Mass drawing an estimated 2.5 million people in Buenos Aires, one of the largest crowds of his papacy. He renewed calls for President Milei's government to protect vulnerable populations amid austerity measures.

events.headline: US House Blocks Floor Vote on Hegseth Impeachment, Refers Articles to Judiciary Committee
events.summary: The US House of Representatives voted to refer articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively blocking an immediate floor vote. The move comes as lawmakers also face a December 11 government shutdown deadline.

events.headline: Eisenkot Urges Netanyahu to Hold Off on Iran Strike Amid Israeli Government Transition
events.summary: Israel's security cabinet reportedly pushed the military to accelerate preparations for a potential strike on Iran, but Chief of Staff Zamir resisted, demanding signed orders and legal backing. On November 11, Gabi Eisenkot — currently attempting to form a government under his 28-day mandate — publicly urged Netanyahu to hold off on security moves during the transition, accusing him of using the prospect of war as political leverage.

events.headline: Indonesia's VP Gibran Formally Resigns, Hands Letter to Assembly
events.summary: Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka personally delivered his resignation letter to the People's Consultative Assembly leadership on November 12, 2026, becoming Indonesia's first directly elected vice president to resign mid-term, hours before the House was due to debate an impeachment petition signed by more than 120 lawmakers. President Prabowo now has 14 days to nominate two successor candidates, and the Assembly's process may take up to 60 days.

events.headline: Salvadoran Troops' Haiti Gang Raid Sparks US Diplomatic Friction Over Coordination
events.summary: Following a raid that killed about 20 gang members at a '400 Mawozo' compound, reports emerged that El Salvador has deployed roughly 2,500 troops in Haiti since mid-October without coordinating with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force. The US charge d'affaires protested the lack of coordination; President Bukele rejected the criticism and Trump backed him, while Secretary Rubio distanced the US from the operation.

events.headline: US Boat Strikes on Alleged Drug Vessels Continue, Cumulative Toll Passes 238
events.summary: The US military's campaign against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, ongoing since September 2025, has killed at least 238 people cumulatively as of mid-November 2026, with additional strikes conducted on November 6 and 10.

events.headline: North Korea Publishes Revised Constitution Dropping Reunification Goal
events.summary: North Korea posted a revised constitution on its Naenara website on November 11, 2026, removing references to reunification and defining South Korea as a separate foreign state. The change reflects the 2023 'two hostile states' declaration and reportedly expands Kim Jong Un's direct authority over the nuclear arsenal, though it stops short of explicitly labeling South Korea 'hostile.'

events.headline: US Measles Outbreak Tops 5,000 Cases With 8 Deaths, Risking Loss of Elimination Status
events.summary: The CDC reported the US measles outbreak has surpassed 5,000 cases, the highest since 1991, with at least eight deaths recorded. Health officials warn the outbreak could cost the United States its measles elimination status if transmission continues past a one-year threshold.

events.headline: Brooklyn Building Collapse Kills Two, Injures Dozens
events.summary: A three-story mixed-use building in Flatbush, Brooklyn collapsed into an adjacent excavation site around 4pm on November 11, 2026, trapping residents and workers. At least two people, including a child, were killed and more than a dozen injured in the collapse.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russia's Largest Oil Refinery in Omsk, 2,500km From Front
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Omsk Oil Refinery, owned by Gazprom Neft and Russia's largest with capacity of about 22 million tonnes a year, on the evening of November 11, 2026, roughly 2,500km from the front line. The strike sparked a fire lasting hours and prompted mobile internet restrictions; it was the third attack on the facility in 2026 following strikes in July and October.

events.headline: Russian Drone Attack Knocks Out Power and Heating in Kryvyi Rih as Grid Strikes Continue
events.summary: A Russian drone attack cut power and heating to parts of Kryvyi Rih overnight, the latest in a sustained campaign against Ukraine's energy grid. The EU has activated its emergency civil protection mechanism in response to the escalating strikes.

events.headline: Qatari PM Makes Unscheduled G7 Stop to Brief Europeans on Iran-US Mediation After Trump Talks
events.summary: Qatar's Prime Minister made an unscheduled stop in Paris to brief G7 counterparts on mediation efforts between the US and Iran, following his meeting with President Trump. European officials expressed cautious optimism about progress on both Iran diplomacy and the Gaza peace plan.

events.headline: PNG Police Identify Chinese Artillery Shell Found in Shipping Container at Port Moresby Wharf
events.summary: A 32kg object found in a shipping container at a Port Moresby wharf construction site around November 3, 2026 was identified by PNG police as an undetonated 130mm Chinese Type 59 artillery projectile containing chemical explosives and a fuse. Four Chinese nationals were arrested; China's embassy claimed the object was a 'wine bottle.' The incident is seen as background to Taiwan's subsequent closure of its PNG representative office.

events.headline: Syria and Saudi Arabia Sign Defense Pact and $403 Million in Loans
events.summary: Syria and Saudi Arabia signed a defense cooperation agreement and $403 million in loans, deepening ties as Damascus rebuilds after years of civil war. Syrian officials separately said they foiled a Hezbollah-linked plot to bomb an oil refinery near Homs.

events.headline: Drone Attack on Iraqi Kurdistan's Khor Mor Gas Field Cuts Regional Power
events.summary: A suspected drone attack on the night of November 8, 2026 sparked a fire and halted production at the Khor Mor gas field, cutting about 2.8 gigawatts — roughly 70-80% of the Kurdistan Region's power supply — affecting Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Duhok and other cities. No group has claimed responsibility, though Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah had referenced the field the day before.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes Kill 12 Civilians, Including a Newborn, Across Four Rakhine Townships
events.summary: Junta airstrikes across four townships in Rakhine State — Kyauktaw, Mrauk-U, Kyaukphyu and Pauktaw — killed at least 12 civilians, including a newborn, in early November 2026. The strikes come as the Arakan Army continues to advance against junta positions in the state.

events.headline: Senegal Migrant Boat Disaster Death Toll Rises to 39
events.summary: The death toll from a migrant boat that capsized off Senegal's coast near Kébémer rose to 39. The vessel was reportedly attempting the dangerous Atlantic route toward Spain's Canary Islands.

events.headline: Colombia Confirms Three Soldiers Dead, 16 Wounded in ELN Drone Attack on Army Base
events.summary: Colombian authorities confirmed three soldiers were killed and 16 wounded in a drone attack on a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolívar. Officials attribute the strike to the ELN, linking it to new reconnaissance drone operations in the region.

events.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent Relocated to Military Base Over Iranian Assassination Threats
events.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was moved to a military base after US officials assessed credible Iranian assassination threats against him. The move comes amid rising tensions between the US and Iran over recent strikes and regional escalation.

events.headline: ICJ Nears Final Ruling on Guyana-Venezuela Essequibo Border Dispute
events.summary: The International Court of Justice is expected to issue a final, binding ruling on the Guyana-Venezuela Essequibo border dispute in late November 2026 or early 2027, after oral hearings concluded in May. Guyana is seeking regional backing from Brazil and Colombia, while Venezuela may not accept a ruling upholding the 1899 Arbitral Award.

events.headline: Venezuela Ends State Monopoly, Opens Power Sector to Private Investment
events.summary: Venezuela's National Assembly passed a law ending the state's decades-old monopoly over electricity generation, allowing private investors contracts of up to 25 years. The move aims to attract capital to rebuild the country's ailing power grid.

events.headline: Boeing to Cut About 2,500 Jobs from Commercial Airplanes Division Amid Production Slowdown
events.summary: Boeing Commercial Airplanes CEO Stephanie Pope told employees November 9 the company will slow production ramp-ups and cut about 5%, roughly 2,500 jobs, from the division's 50,500 workers through layoffs and attrition. It is Boeing's first commercial-division cuts in nearly two years, with affected staff to be notified in December.

events.headline: Airstrikes Near Yemen's Capital Sanaa Kill at Least 27 Amid Houthi-Government Fighting
events.summary: Airstrikes near Sanaa killed at least 27 people in Al-Shariya village, as Yemeni government forces reported battlefield advances. Houthi officials said missile and drone attacks also struck Saudi oil sites and Riyadh's airport.

events.headline: Fresh Insurgent Violence Displaces Over 7,000 in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado
events.summary: The International Organization for Migration confirms more than 7,000 people have fled their homes in Cabo Delgado province since late September amid a new wave of attacks, abductions and roadblocks by ISIS-linked insurgents. The violence is active across nine districts of the province.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrike on Resistance Hospital Kills Five Health Workers
events.summary: A junta airstrike on a resistance-run hospital in Hlyawhpyukone village, Kawlin Township, Sagaing Region, killed five health workers on November 4, 2026, including senior physician Dr. Zar Ni Tun. WHO Director-General Tedros confirmed the attack, noting Myanmar's 2026 total of attacks on healthcare has reached 65, with 63 deaths; further junta strikes on schools in Sagaing killed 11 people on November 10.

events.headline: Israel Widens Strikes on Hezbollah Positions Across Five Southern Lebanon Villages
events.summary: Israel intensified airstrikes on suspected Hezbollah positions across five villages in southern Lebanon, days after a strike killed three sisters and their grandmother in Aynata. Lebanese residents are stocking up on supplies amid fears of further escalation despite a framework ceasefire deal.

events.headline: Eurozone Inflation Hits 4% in October, Double the ECB's Target
events.summary: Eurostat data showed annual eurozone inflation rose to 4% in October from 3.8% in September, the highest since September 2023, driven by a 20.8% year-on-year jump in energy prices. The reading strengthens the case for an ECB rate hike in December after the bank held rates at 2.5% on October 29.

events.headline: Sudanese Army Reports Gains Against RSF in West Kordofan Offensive
events.summary: Sudan's army said it made territorial gains against the Rapid Support Forces in the El-Khwei area of West Kordofan, as fighting in the region intensifies. The advance follows weeks of escalating clashes that prompted Ethiopia to expel Sudanese diplomats.

events.headline: Bangladesh Rejects Sheikh Hasina's Passport Request Ahead of Planned December Return
events.summary: Bangladesh's government denied ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's request for a new passport from its High Commission in Delhi, where she has sought refuge in India. Officials said they would not provide travel documents to a 'terrorist' ahead of her reportedly planned December return.

events.headline: Montana DOJ Investigates Alleged Vote-Tampering by Public Service Commission in Energy Rate Case
events.summary: Montana's Department of Justice is reviewing whether a Public Service Commission vote in a NorthWestern Energy rate case — involving the same commission that approved NorthWestern's $15.4B merger with Black Hills Corp. — was improperly recorded. Commissioner Pinocci alleges his 'no' vote was changed to 'yes' without consent, while PSC President Welborn denies any vote was altered, raising a fresh credibility controversy for the commission.

events.headline: Fog Triggers Fatal 86-Vehicle Pile-Up on Bulgaria's Trakia Motorway, 12 Dead
events.summary: Dense fog caused two multi-vehicle pile-ups involving about 86 vehicles near Zimnitsa and Yambol on the morning of November 10, 2026. Twelve people were killed and 46 to 51 injured, prompting Bulgaria to declare a day of national mourning.

events.headline: France Formally Blames Iran for Cyberattack on Supermarket Refrigeration Systems
events.summary: France formally accused Iran of orchestrating a cyberattack that disrupted refrigeration systems at supermarkets across the country. The incident adds to a string of alleged Iranian cyber operations against European infrastructure amid rising tensions over Iran's nuclear and regional activities.

events.headline: US Army Officer Arrested in UK on Suspicion of Spying for Russia
events.summary: British authorities arrested a US Army officer near Gloucester on suspicion of espionage for Russia. The arrest adds to heightened concerns about Russian intelligence activity in the UK amid the ongoing war in Ukraine.

events.headline: TTP Militants Ambush Police Convoy Near Kohat, Pakistan, Killing About 11 Officers
events.summary: TTP-linked militants ambushed a police convoy in the Gumbat area between Kohat and Karak districts, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on November 11, 2026, as officers headed to raid illegal mining operations. At least 10-11 police, including DSP Haider Zaman, were killed and 12 wounded; authorities reported 18 militants also died.

events.headline: New Mexico Flood Recovery Costs Top $200 Million After Record San Juan River Flooding
events.summary: Late-October/early-November flooding sent the San Juan River at Farmington from about 3.5 feet to 14 feet in roughly a day, destroying at least 64 homes and damaging hundreds more, with more than 5,000 residents evacuated. Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham has signed 73 emergency executive orders and released over $54 million in state recovery funds; total recovery costs could reach $200-300 million.

events.headline: Lawsuit Filed to Block Washington State's Transgender Student-Athlete Initiative 638
events.summary: On Nov. 9, TransFamilies, the Washington Education Association, ACLU of Washington, and parents of both cisgender and transgender student-athletes filed suit in King County Superior Court seeking to block voter-approved Initiative 638, which requires sex verification for girls' school sports before its Dec. 3 effective date. The suit alleges violations of the state constitution's privacy, equal-rights, and education-access provisions.

events.headline: Poland Orders Review of Gun Laws After Kraków's First Mass Shooting
events.summary: Polish Prime Minister Tusk ordered a review of the country's gun laws following a mass shooting in Kraków described as the country's first, which authorities are treating as a terrorist attack. Ministers have floated tighter firearm controls in response.

events.headline: More Than 50,000 Flee Into Kenya as Ethiopia's Oromia-Somali Border Clashes Escalate
events.summary: More than 50,000 people have fled into Kenya to escape deadly clashes along the Oromia-Somali regional border near Moyale, Ethiopia. The violence is distinct from the separate conflict-driven health crisis in Ethiopia's Amhara region.

events.headline: Suspected Al-Shabaab Ambush Kills Eight Road Workers in Mandera, Kenya
events.summary: Gunmen ambushed a security escort guarding a road construction project on the Mandera-Arabia-Lafey road around 7am on November 10, 2026, killing five road workers, two national police reservists and a driver. Attackers are believed to have crossed from neighboring Somalia.

events.headline: Spain Holds First Joint General Strike Since 2012 Over Housing Costs Ahead of Election
events.summary: Spanish unions CCOO and UGT led a nationwide general strike over soaring housing costs and cost-of-living pressures, the first joint walkout of its kind since 2012. The action comes two weeks before Spain's November 29 snap election.

events.headline: St. Louis House Fire Kills 2-Year-Old Girl, Five Hospitalized in Carondelet Neighborhood
events.summary: A predawn fire around 4 a.m. Nov. 11 in the Carondelet neighborhood killed a 2-year-old girl and sent two adults and three children to the hospital for smoke exposure. The home reportedly had no electricity, residents were using candles and a small heater, and there were no working smoke detectors.

events.headline: Oklahoma Supreme Court Strikes Down Initiative-Petition Restriction Law SB 1027
events.summary: In a 5-4 ruling issued Nov. 10, the Oklahoma Supreme Court held SB 1027 unconstitutional and void in its entirety. The court found its registered-voter requirement for petition circulators, county signature caps, and ban on incentive pay for circulators violated First Amendment protections for political speech and the right to petition.

events.headline: Ninth Circuit Partially Blocks California's SB 253/SB 261 Climate-Disclosure Laws
events.summary: A divided Ninth Circuit panel ruled Nov. 9 in Chamber of Commerce v. Sanchez that SB 253's Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse-gas reporting may proceed, but found SB 253's Scope 3 supply-chain emissions reporting and SB 261's climate-risk financial disclosure requirement likely unconstitutional as compelled speech. The case returns to district court on severability; this is a preliminary-injunction ruling, not a final judgment.

events.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill at Least Seven Palestinians in Gaza Despite Ceasefire
events.summary: Israeli attacks killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza, including a father and son, despite a ceasefire agreement in place. Medics in Gaza City reported continued casualties from sporadic strikes.

events.headline: Dublin Hosts Ninth European Political Community Summit With About 50 Leaders
events.summary: The European Political Community convened its ninth summit in Dublin on November 12, 2026, co-chaired by EU Council President Antonio Costa and Irish Taoiseach Micheal Martin under the theme 'Europe - strong, secure and connected.' About 50 leaders attended, including Zelensky, Macron and Merz, with the Ukraine war dominating the agenda.

events.headline: Egypt's $8bn IMF Program Nears December Expiry Amid Pound Weakness
events.summary: Egypt's $8 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility is set to expire on December 15, 2026, with a final review potentially releasing about $2.3 billion; Cairo says it will not seek a new IMF program afterward. The Egyptian pound fell about 8% in October amid capital outflows, even as Egypt signed a new $1 billion World Bank deal, including a $200 million UK credit guarantee, in early November.

events.headline: Americas Region Risks Losing Measles Elimination Status Amid Regional Resurgence
events.summary: A PAHO commission is reviewing through November 13 whether the US, Mexico, Guatemala, Peru and Bolivia retain their measles elimination status after 57,666 confirmed cases were recorded across 17 countries in the Americas from January to October 2026.
events.locationName: Americas (regional, PAHO review in Washington, D.C.)

events.headline: Indonesia Police Chief Says Illegal Wiretapping of Prabowo Extended to Many Others
events.summary: Police chief Gen. Suyudi Ario Seto told a parliamentary hearing on November 12, 2026 that illegal wiretapping targeting President Prabowo also extended to cabinet officials, politicians, activists, journalists and law enforcement figures. The scandal emerged after three senior generals, including Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, the president's chief of staff, were detained.

events.headline: Shapiro Pledges $15 Minimum Wage, Abortion-Rights Codification After Democrats Win Pennsylvania Trifecta
events.summary: Pennsylvania Democrats won control of the governorship, House and Senate for the first time since 1993. Gov. Josh Shapiro pledged his first priority bills will raise the minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour and codify abortion rights into state law.

events.headline: Auto Supplier Dakkota to Close Detroit Plant, Cutting 397 Jobs
events.summary: Dakkota Integrated Systems is closing its Detroit instrument-panel plant in two phases, on December 31, 2026 and March 31, 2027, after losing Stellantis contracts for the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The closure will eliminate 397 jobs.

events.headline: Brazil's Real Slides as Lula Government Readies Fiscal-Adjustment Package
events.summary: Brazil's currency weakened as President Lula's economic team prepared a fiscal-adjustment package worth an estimated 50-60 billion reais for 2027 to calm market concerns over high interest rates and spending. Lula pledged budget discipline amid investor jitters.

events.headline: Democrat Joe Madge Ousts Incoming South Carolina House Majority Leader Caskey After Recount
events.summary: A mandatory recount certified Nov. 11 confirmed Democrat Joe Madge defeated Republican incumbent and incoming House Majority Leader Micah Caskey by 106 votes (7,263 to 7,157) in deep-red Lexington County's House District 89.

events.headline: Florida Democrats Break GOP House Supermajority After Brevard County Recount
events.summary: A machine recount finalized this week confirmed Democrat Dan McDow defeated Republican incumbent Monique Miller by 286 votes in Florida House District 33, flipping a seat Republicans had held for over a decade and giving Democrats 50 of 120 Florida House seats, ending the GOP supermajority.

events.headline: Ohio Governor DeWine Weighing Clemency for 13 Death Row Inmates Before Leaving Office
events.summary: Ohio's parole board is reviewing clemency recommendations for 13 death row inmates at Gov. Mike DeWine's request before he leaves office. DeWine, who helped write Ohio's 1981 capital punishment law, called for abolishing the death penalty in June and has commuted only one sentence in nearly eight years in office; prosecutors in multiple counties oppose the effort.

events.headline: Dozens of Immigrant Children in Kansas City Face Fast-Tracked Deportation
events.summary: At least two dozen immigrant children in the Kansas City area, ages 9-17, are in active removal proceedings after USCIS rescinded deferred-action protections for new/renewal Special Immigrant Juvenile status applications effective May 2026. Some hearings originally docketed for 2027 have been moved up to mid-November; nationwide roughly 150,000 youths with SIJ status may be affected.

events.headline: Arizona New World Screwworm Outbreak Grows to Six Confirmed Cases
events.summary: Since the first case was confirmed Oct. 28 in Elfrida, Arizona has confirmed six New World screwworm cases (in horses, dogs, and a ram) across Cochise, Graham and Greenlee counties, most recently a horse near Pearce on Nov. 10. USDA is releasing millions of sterile flies and counties have established quarantine zones with travel restrictions for pets and livestock.

events.headline: Texas Governor-Elect Hinojosa's Agenda Takes Shape as GOP Supreme Court Justice Weighs Retirement
events.summary: Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa is pushing a $1,500-per-household rebate from the Rainy Day Fund, a cost-of-living emergency declaration, and an electricity-rate freeze, while a separate Democratic-filed bill would pursue a high-speed rail public-private partnership along I-35. Republican Texas Supreme Court Justice Debra Lehrmann is reportedly considering early retirement, which, combined with other GOP justices' election losses, could let Hinojosa flip the court's majority to Democrats.

events.headline: Utah Governor Cox Says GOP Suffered 'Historic Defeat' as Democrats End Republican Supermajority
events.summary: Utah's Republican legislative supermajority, held since 1998, was broken in the Nov. 2026 election, with roughly 16 GOP seats lost to Democrats and unaffiliated candidates — the largest partisan swing of any state. Gov. Spencer Cox called it a 'historic defeat,' attributing it partly to the legislature ignoring voters on redistricting.

events.headline: Kraft Group's Proposed $16 Billion Data Center Campus Draws Resident Pushback in Sutton, Massachusetts
events.summary: The Kraft Group and Unified Global Packaging Group proposed a roughly $16 billion, 900MW, multi-building data center campus in Sutton. At a Nov. 10 Select Board meeting, residents voiced noise concerns and pushed for a possible moratorium; the board deferred a vote pending further public forums.

events.headline: Federal Government Blocks About $113 Million in Minnesota Medicaid Reimbursements Over Fraud Concerns
events.summary: CMS, under the Trump administration, will not reimburse Minnesota for nearly $113 million spent on Medicaid provider payments flagged as high fraud-risk, denying 78 of 330 claims reviewed for issues like missing documentation and unsigned provider agreements. It is part of a larger $550 million in frozen Medicaid funds; Minnesota AG Keith Ellison's office is challenging the deferrals in court.

events.headline: Cherokee Nation Council Votes Unanimously to Oppose $4 Billion Inola, Oklahoma Aluminum Smelter
events.summary: The 17-member Cherokee Nation Tribal Council unanimously passed a resolution, reported Nov. 11, backing the neighboring Muscogee Nation's opposition to the proposed $4 billion Century Aluminum/Emirates Global Aluminum smelter near Inola. The resolution cites cross-border pollution concerns and calls for full tribal consultation; the project has support from Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt and the state government.

events.headline: Three Washington School Districts Prepare to Sue State Over $800 Million Funding Shortfall
events.summary: Lake Washington and Tacoma school boards passed resolutions Oct. 22, and Yakima followed Nov. 2, authorizing participation in a prospective lawsuit alleging the state has fallen out of compliance with its McCleary-era obligation to fully fund basic education. The districts cite an estimated $800 million shortfall forcing layoffs, larger class sizes, and reliance on local levies; no lawsuit has been filed yet as of Nov. 9.

events.headline: Teamsters Strike at Associated Grocers Northeast Disrupts New England Grocery Deliveries
events.summary: More than 250 Teamsters Local 633 members have been on strike since early November at Associated Grocers Northeast's Pembroke, New Hampshire distribution center after their contract expired October 17, with pensions a key sticking point. The strike has caused delivery delays and shelf shortages at grocery stores across New Hampshire, Vermont, Maine and upstate New York.

events.headline: Pennsylvania Secures Record $7.8 Million Child-Labor Settlement with Walmart
events.summary: The Shapiro administration announced a $7.8 million settlement with Walmart, the largest child-labor enforcement action in Pennsylvania history, after audits found an average of 65 violations at each of eight stores. The deal requires compliance reforms across Walmart's Pennsylvania locations.

events.headline: West Virginia State Auditor Faces Federal Grand Jury Subpoena Over Tax Deed Scandal
events.summary: State Auditor Mark Hunt confirmed he received a federal grand jury subpoena after a WV Watch investigation found he personally signed nine tax deeds benefiting a friend's company. West Virginia Democrats are calling for an immediate investigation.

events.headline: Suniva Begins Construction on $600 Million Solar Cell Plant in Laurens County, South Carolina
events.summary: Suniva broke ground on a 4.5 GW solar-cell manufacturing facility backed by an $835 million capital raise, expected to create about 560 jobs by 2028. The expansion would bring Suniva's total US production capacity to 5.5 GW.

events.headline: Peace River Flooding Inundates Homes in Arcadia, Florida's DeSoto County
events.summary: The Peace River crested at major flood stage of about 16 feet 4 inches, sending waist-high water into the River Acres neighborhood of Arcadia and flooding dozens of homes, buildings and vehicles. About 100 animals were evacuated from a nearby wildlife park as floodwaters began to recede.

events.headline: Kansas Governor's Race Remains Uncalled a Week After Election as Mandatory Audit Proceeds
events.summary: Democrat Cindy Holscher leads Republican Ty Masterson by about 7,000 votes, a margin under 1% that triggered a mandatory close-race audit in the Kansas governor's race. The recount deadline is November 17, with five other races also under audit.

events.headline: Illinois Governor Pritzker Appeals FEMA's Denial of Disaster Aid for Flood-Hit Counties
events.summary: Gov. JB Pritzker appealed FEMA's denial of disaster assistance for eight Illinois counties hit by August flooding, tornadoes and high winds, submitting updated damage estimates of $43 million versus FEMA's $24.9 million threshold. The appeal has bipartisan support from 18 state lawmakers.

events.headline: Trona Workers Rally Against WE Soda's Plan to Cut 350 Jobs in Sweetwater County, Wyoming
events.summary: WE Soda plans to cut about 350 jobs, shrinking its Westvaco trona mine workforce from roughly 850 to 500 over two years, as it shifts from underground to in-situ solution mining amid cheap Chinese soda-ash exports. More than 100 workers and community members rallied on November 9, saying no severance has been offered.

events.headline: Powerful Windstorm Cuts Power to Over 100,000 in Western Washington as Second Atmospheric River Approaches
events.summary: A cold front brought wind gusts up to 69-95 mph overnight November 7-8, knocking out power to between 100,000 and 115,000 customers across western Washington. A second, stronger atmospheric river was moving into the Puget Sound region November 9-10 with warnings of major flooding risk.

events.headline: Colombia Probes Alleged Plan by Intelligence Agency to Spy on Ex-Presidents Under Petro
events.summary: Leaked documents allege Colombia's DNI intelligence agency planned to spy on former presidents and interfere in elections during the Petro administration. Prosecutors have opened an investigation into the allegations.

events.headline: Record Rainfall Triggers Deadly Floods and Landslides Across Central Vietnam
events.summary: Record-breaking rainfall triggered widespread flooding and landslides across central Vietnam, affecting Da Nang, Hue and Quang Tri provinces. Authorities ordered flood preparations as rainfall records were shattered in multiple provinces.

events.headline: Indiana Child Welfare Agency Says It Needs $300 Million Emergency State Infusion
events.summary: DCS Director Jennifer Dorfmeyer told Indiana's State Budget Committee on Nov. 11 that the agency expects to need a $300 million infusion to its main account for fiscal year 2027, continuing a pattern of recent-year shortfalls. She described a new service-utilization review team as a mitigation step.

events.headline: West Virginia Governor Announces $17B Gas Plants, $7.5B Coal Plant Upgrades
events.summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey announced Nov. 12 that Appalachian Power will invest $17 billion in three new natural gas-fired plants (3 GW total, operational by 2031) and $7.5 billion to upgrade coal-fired plants through 2050. The gas buildout is projected to create about 2,050 construction jobs and 100 permanent jobs across multiple West Virginia sites.

events.headline: Wisconsin Supreme Court Agrees 5-1 to Hear Union Challenge to Act 10
events.summary: The Wisconsin Supreme Court ruled 5-1 to hear a lawsuit, led by the Abbotsford Education Association, challenging 2011's Act 10 collective-bargaining restrictions, arguing carve-outs exempting some public-safety unions violate the state constitution's equal protection clause. Briefing is due Dec. 11, with a decision expected before next summer.

events.headline: Chad-Niger Drone Strike Dispute Escalates; Algeria Sends Mediator
events.summary: Niger accuses Chad, and alleges French support, of an October 24 drone strike that killed two civilians in Emi Lulu, Agadez region; Chad denies involvement and is demanding evidence or an independent probe. Algeria's President Tebboune dispatched Foreign Minister Attaf as an envoy to N'Djamena and Niamey on November 3-4, and Niger has also raised the issue at the UN Security Council.

events.headline: Storm Charles Joins Storm Bruna, Extending Flood Alerts From Iberia Toward France and Italy
events.summary: After Portugal declared a nationwide state of alert, storms Bruna and Charles brought red warnings, up to 300mm of rainfall and flood and landslide risk across western and southern Spain and Portugal through November 10-12. The system is extending into southeastern France and northern Italy's Adriatic coast on November 12 as it weakens.

events.headline: UNIFIL Patrol Comes Under Fire Near Wadi Jilu in Southern Lebanon
events.summary: A UNIFIL patrol came under fire — about a dozen rounds — on the evening of November 10, 2026 near Wadi Jilu in Lebanon's Tyre district. Peacekeepers returned fire after seeing a muzzle flash; no casualties were reported, and UNIFIL called the incident a violation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701, urging a Lebanese investigation. No group has claimed responsibility.

events.headline: Russia Says It Detained Two Alleged Polish Spies in Kaliningrad; Poland Calls It a Provocation
events.summary: Russia's FSB announced on November 11, 2026 — Poland's Independence Day — that it had detained two alleged Polish spies in the Kaliningrad region. Poland dismissed the claims as a provocation and said it was still verifying the information.

events.headline: Hoax Bomb Threat Emails Trigger Evacuations at Thousands of Italian Schools
events.summary: A coordinated anonymous email signed 'Mikhail Andropov' triggered bomb-threat alerts at about 6,300 Italian schools on November 11, 2026, with roughly 312 schools materially evacuated. Similar hoax threats hit schools in the UK and Ireland; the same alias has previously been used against broadcasters including RTE, Bulgaria's Nova TV and Sky News.

events.headline: Philadelphia Teachers Union Proposes $25M Alternative Plan to Keep 17 Schools Open
events.summary: The Philadelphia Federation of Teachers released a facilities plan proposing roughly $25.35 million in immediate repairs, maintenance and cleaning to keep 17 schools open, versus the district's closure plan. The union's plan targets 'fair' building condition by 2029 and 'good' condition by 2031; the district says the proposal falls short given declining enrollment and a $298M repair need at those buildings.

events.headline: New York Launches AI Safety Research Center at SUNY Binghamton, Announces $100M Road Repaving
events.summary: On Nov. 10, Gov. Hochul launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at SUNY Binghamton, involving 80+ researchers co-led by Cornell Tech's Greg Morrisett and Columbia's Jeannette Wing. She separately announced $100 million for repaving 642 lane-miles statewide via the Harsh Winter Paving program.

events.headline: Maryland Prison Inmate Death at North Branch Correctional Institution Investigated as Possible Homicide
events.summary: An inmate was pronounced dead just before midnight Nov. 9 at the 'hypermax' North Branch Correctional Institution in Cumberland. The Maryland State Police Homicide Unit is investigating, with two fellow inmates identified as suspects but not yet charged pending autopsy results.

events.headline: Israeli Settlers Seize Eight Palestinian Homes Near Jericho, Displacing Dozens
events.summary: About 30 armed settlers affiliated with the Nachala movement took over eight Palestinian homes in Ein al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, on November 4-5, 2026, displacing roughly 70 residents. Settlers claim the properties were legally purchased, while the Palestinian Authority says the documents were forged; Peace Now reports settlers assaulted two Israeli activists and shot a Palestinian man, and the UN has condemned the seizure.

events.headline: Italy's Governing Coalition Splits Over Continued Aid to Ukraine Amid Abu Dhabi Talks
events.summary: Italy's ruling coalition is divided over whether to continue military aid to Ukraine, as debate intensifies alongside US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi. The disagreement reflects wider European uncertainty over the war's endgame.

events.headline: Wild River Fire in New Hampshire's White Mountain National Forest Now Over Half Contained
events.summary: The Wild River Fire, burning since Nov. 1 about 7 miles southeast of Gorham, NH, is now roughly 53-59% contained after burning 817-821 acres, aided by wet weather. The U.S. Forest Service says it is the largest wildfire in the White Mountain National Forest since 1918 and is human-caused, under investigation; the area remains closed to visitors.

events.headline: Wisconsin Democrats Elect Greta Neubauer First Female Assembly Speaker; GOP Names Julian Bradley Senate Minority Leader
events.summary: On Nov. 11, Wisconsin Democrats elected Dianne Hesselbein Senate Majority Leader and Greta Neubauer the Assembly's first-ever female Speaker, giving women the top posts in both chambers for the first time. Republicans named Julian Bradley Senate Minority Leader, the first Black lawmaker to lead a caucus in either chamber.

events.headline: Oklahoma Awarded $227M in Year-Two Federal Rural Health Transformation Funding
events.summary: CMS/HHS announced $10 billion in second-year Rural Health Transformation Program awards to all 50 states on Nov. 9, with Oklahoma receiving approximately $227.1 million, up from $223.5 million in year one. The program will support 29 programs and more than 500 organizations statewide.

events.headline: Washington Lands Commissioner Seeks Permanent $60M/Year Wildfire Funding After Historic 2026 Fire Season
events.summary: As Washington's 2026 wildfire season officially ended, Commissioner of Public Lands Dave Upthegrove and the Department of Natural Resources are pressing the legislature to fully fund 2027 fire prevention and suppression efforts, seeking to lock in a $60 million annual commitment following one of the state's most severe fire seasons in recent years.

events.headline: Settler Attack Injures Six Civil Rights Activists in West Bank Village of Qusra
events.summary: Israeli settlers attacked and injured six civil rights activists in the West Bank village of Qusra, according to rights groups. The incident is part of a continuing pattern of settler violence against Palestinians and activists in the occupied territory.

events.headline: Argentina's Economy Enters Technical Recession as Country Risk Eases
events.summary: Argentina's country-risk index fell to 852 basis points on November 11, its third consecutive daily decline, even as GDP contracted 0.6% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 2026, the first contraction since 2024. A further Q3 contraction of about 1.5% is forecast, implying a technical recession that poses a political test for President Milei ahead of 2027 elections.

events.headline: Canada's Carney Government Unveils $142 Billion Budget 2026
events.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney's second federal budget, unveiled November 5, 2026, includes $142.1 billion in new spending and measures over five years, including a $36 billion productivity deduction, a $4.6 billion grocery rebate boost and $11.2 billion to end homelessness within a decade. The budget projects a $62.3 billion deficit for the current fiscal year.

events.headline: Cargo Ship Carrying Steel Sinks Off Jiangsu Coast in Storm, All 14 Crew Rescued
events.summary: A steel-carrying cargo ship sank in the southern Yellow Sea off China's Jiangsu coast on November 9, 2026 after flooding and tilting in a storm with level-8 winds and four-meter waves. China's East China Sea Rescue Bureau used helicopters and a rescue vessel to save all 14 crew members, who were taken to Binhai Port in Yancheng.

events.headline: US Congress Returns for Lame-Duck Session Facing Dec 11 Shutdown Deadline
events.summary: The 119th Congress returned in early November 2026 for a lame-duck session with government funding set to expire on December 11, 2026. None of the 12 required appropriations bills have passed, raising the risk of what would be the fourth government shutdown of Trump's second term.

events.headline: Indonesian Police Detain 154 After Violent Yogyakarta Protests Over Economy
events.summary: Police detained 154 people after protests near Yogyakarta's parliament turned violent overnight on November 11-12, 2026, with protesters throwing rocks, firecrackers and Molotov cocktails against tear gas and water cannon. Similar unrest was seen in Surabaya, driven by grievances over stagnant wages, rising living costs and ongoing wildfires.

events.headline: Five Killed, Dozens Injured in Three-Bus Collision on Sri Lanka's A9 Highway
events.summary: Two state-run buses collided head-on near the Rambewa-Welioya junction in Anuradhapura district on November 10, 2026, and a third private bus then crashed into the wreckage. Five people were killed and between 40 and 70 injured.

events.headline: ELN Bomb Threats Force Evacuation of Major Colombian TV and Radio Outlets
events.summary: Colombia's Caracol Television and Radio evacuated staff after bomb threats attributed to the ELN guerrilla group targeting major media outlets. The Committee to Protect Journalists called on authorities to ensure the safety of newsroom staff.

events.headline: Ecuador's Assembly Grants President Noboa Leave to Campaign Ahead of Nov 29 Local Elections
events.summary: Ecuador's National Assembly approved a campaign leave for President Daniel Noboa ahead of the November 29 local and provincial elections. The move comes amid ongoing political tension, including protests over the detention of opposition leader Luisa González.

events.headline: Lima Bus Companies Suspend Routes in Mass Protest Against Extortion Violence
events.summary: More than 50 transport companies suspended service in Lima to protest rampant extortion, which Peruvian authorities say has killed 93 transit workers since January. The strike disrupted commuting across the capital.

events.headline: Thailand Keeps Cambodia Border Closed Indefinitely, Steps Up Security Patrols
events.summary: Thailand announced it will keep its border with Cambodia closed indefinitely, citing continued security concerns, while increasing military patrols in the area. The closure extends a standoff between the two neighbors following earlier border clashes.

events.headline: Solomon Islands PM Matthew Wale Recovering in Australia After Medical Treatment
events.summary: Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was flown to Australia for urgent medical treatment and is now recovering, while his government advances constitutional reforms aimed at ending unstable coalition politics. The event is unrelated to a recent magnitude 6.4 earthquake that struck the Solomon Islands.
